profile.summary: TranscriptFormer is a family of generative single-cell foundation models trained on up to 112 million cells from 12 species. It reads a cell's raw counts (genes by Ensembl ID) and models gene identities and expression levels jointly; its cell embeddings are used for cross-species cell type classification, disease state identification and transfer of annotations, and the generative model can be prompted for cell type-specific transcription factors and gene-gene interactions.

summary_quotes.text: a family of generative foundation models trained on up to 112 million cells spanning 1.53 billion years of evolution across 12 species
By jointly modeling gene identities and expression levels using a novel generative architecture
The model expects unnormalized count data (raw counts)
TranscriptFormer can be prompted to predict cell type-specific transcription factors and gene-gene interactions

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: TranscriptFormer is a generative autoregressive joint model over genes and their expression levels in a cell, built on a transformer with coupled gene and transcript heads, expression-aware multi-head self-attention, causal masking and a count likelihood. The README says the non-trainable parameters come from frozen pretrained embeddings, that each model comes with protein embeddings for its training species, and that protein embeddings for new species can be generated with ESM-2. Cell embeddings are mean-pooled over the genes of a cell; contextual gene embeddings are the per-gene transformer outputs.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: Three models are released: TF-Metazoa (12 species, 112 million cells), TF-Exemplar (human and four model organisms, 110 million cells) and TF-Sapiens (57 million human cells). They differ in trainable parameters and vocabulary size. Weights are downloaded from AWS S3 with the transcriptformer download command; no checksum or version label is given for them in the README. A result should name the model, the package version and the commit.

**TF-Exemplar**: Trained on 110 million cells from human and four model organisms
**TF-Sapiens**: Trained on 57 million human-only cells.

sections.title: Intended uses
sections.body: Zero-shot cell type classification in and across species, disease state identification in human cells, annotation transfer, and prompting for transcription factors and gene-gene relations. Out-of-distribution species can be embedded with protein embeddings for 24 species provided, or new ones generated with ESM-2.

quotes.text: TranscriptFormer can also perform zero-shot disease state identification in human cells and accurately transfers cell state annotations across species boundaries
Out of the box, there are 24 species with protein embeddings available for download
TranscriptFormer is a family of generative foundation models representing a cross-species generative cell atlas

run_guide.summary: Install transcriptformer, download the TF-Sapiens weights and embed the repository's human test file.
prerequisites: Python 3.11 or newer and the uv package manager.
A GPU (A100 40GB recommended; 16GB works with batch size 1-4).

steps.title: Get the code and install
steps.shell:
git clone https://github.com/czi-ai/transcriptformer.git
cd transcriptformer
git checkout --detach 2ce3b4aa071192202ae30cbc9f91b33c6d8be2ed
uv venv --python=3.11
source .venv/bin/activate
uv pip install -e .
steps.explanation: The README's install from source; the checkout line is added by Rewire to pin the reviewed commit. Installing from source gives the test data used below.

quotes.text: git clone https://github.com/czi-ai/transcriptformer.git
uv venv --python=3.11
uv pip install -e .
